sections.h2: What kind of city is Montgomery, Alabama, for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Montgomery is the capital of Alabama and the county seat of Montgomery County, built beside the Alabama River on the Gulf Coastal Plain. The city was named for Revolutionary War general Richard Montgomery, and the Census Bureau counted 200,603 residents in 2020, which made it the fourth most populous city in the state.

That mix of state government, a large air force base and heavy manufacturing gives the housing stock a wide range. A downtown condo near the Capitol, a mid-century brick ranch on the east side and a farmhouse on the edge of town all sit inside one city limit that covers about 160 square miles of land.

Sellers here tend to face a few recurring situations. Houses are inherited from relatives who lived in the same neighborhood for decades, rental properties age out, and owners who were transferred in or out of Maxwell Air Force Base need a quick closing date. Each of those has its own timing problem, and the sections below tie the local facts to them.

sections.h2: How big is Montgomery and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Montgomery covers 162.27 square miles, of which 159.86 is land, and its elevation is roughly 240 feet. Downtown lies on the south bank of the Alabama River, about six miles downstream from the point where the Coosa and Tallapoosa rivers meet.

sections.h2: What happened to Montgomery in its early history, and does it still show in the housing?
sections.html:
Montgomery formed in 1819 when two river towns, Alabama Town and New Philadelphia, merged under one charter. Its founders set aside a hilltop called Goat Hill for a future capitol, and the legislature moved the state capital here from Tuscaloosa in 1846.

In 1886 Montgomery became the first American city to run citywide electric streetcars, nicknamed the Lightning Route. Residents followed those lines outward to what were then suburbs, so older neighborhoods sit along former streetcar corridors instead of around a single center.

The city also adopted a downtown master plan in 2007, covering Court Square, the riverfront and Dexter Avenue, and it was one of the first cities in the country to use SmartCode zoning. Owners near downtown should expect that zoning rules can differ from those in the outer subdivisions.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers in Montgomery?
sections.html:
The largest employers in Montgomery are Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base and the State of Alabama. According to the city's 2022 annual financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, the top of the list looks like this:

Government work gives the local market stability, but it also creates predictable churn. Military families rotate on assignment cycles, and a house that cannot close before a report date becomes a carrying cost across two cities.

Healthcare adds another layer. Baptist Medical Center South, Baptist Medical Center East near Auburn University at Montgomery, and Jackson Hospital beside Oak Park off Interstate 85 all anchor their own surrounding streets.

sections.h2: What does Montgomery weather do to a house?
sections.html:
Montgomery has a humid subtropical climate, with long, hot summers and short, mild winters, and the weather leaves a clear mark on roofs, cooling systems and crawl spaces. The July daily average is about 82 degrees, highs top 90 on roughly 86 days a year, and afternoon heat index readings frequently reach 100.

Rain adds to the wear. The city averages about 51 inches of precipitation a year, and February, March and July are the wettest months. Here is what that means in practice:

  • Roofs take heat for months and then spring hail and wind. Roof condition is a standard inspection item.
  • Air conditioning runs hard from May through September, so a failing unit is one of the first things a buyer's inspector flags.
  • Humidity near 70 percent on average encourages mold, wood rot and soft spots under sinks and around windows.
  • Severe thunderstorms can bring large hail, and tropical storms that weaken after reaching the Gulf Coast can drop heavy rain on the area.

Montgomery also has a tornado history. A storm struck the western part of the city on February 12, 1945, killing 26 people and injuring 293.

sections.h2: Which schools and campuses influence where people want to live in Montgomery?
sections.html:
Most of the city is served by Montgomery Public Schools, which enrolled 26,381 students in 2022 and runs 32 elementary schools, 13 middle schools and 10 high schools, plus six magnet schools. Magnet programs are part of the system, so school assignment is one factor buyers weigh.

Maxwell Air Force Base residents are zoned to a Department of Defense school for grades K through 8 and then to Montgomery Public Schools for high school.

Higher education is a second source of demand. Montgomery has three public universities, Alabama State University, Troy University's Montgomery campus and Auburn University at Montgomery, plus two private colleges, Faulkner University and Huntingdon College. Those campuses bring students and staff who need housing nearby.

sections.h2: How do people get around Montgomery?
sections.html:
Montgomery sits on two interstates. Interstate 65 runs through the city and Interstate 85 ends there, and several major rail lines also pass through, although passenger rail service stopped in 1995. Montgomery Regional Airport offers regular flights to Atlanta, Houston and Charlotte.

For a seller, road access mostly shows up in the price conversation. A house a few minutes from an interstate ramp reaches the base, the downtown offices and the hospitals quickly, while a property on a busy arterial or beside a rail line may need more negotiation. A cash buyer looks at those traits the same way a conventional buyer does, then folds any needed repairs into the offer.

sections.h2: What do Montgomery sellers pay at recording, and when is property tax due?
sections.html:
Alabama collects a deed recordation tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, and it must be paid before the probate office will record the deed. Under Alabama Code section 40-22-1, the judge of probate calculates it from the actual purchase price, and the deed has to be accompanied by proof of that price on a form the Department of Revenue provides.

As an illustration of the rate only, a $150,000 sale works out to $150 of recordation tax under that formula, before any recording fee, and only the value above a mortgage on which mortgage tax was already paid is taxed. A title company or closing attorney normally sorts out the exact figure.

Property tax is a separate matter. The Alabama Department of Revenue says property taxes are due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. If you sell in the fall, ask who pays the bill, because the amount is usually split at closing by the dates in the contract.

Check the Montgomery County appraisal and tax offices for your parcel's figures and any exemptions, since those depend on the property and the owner.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Montgomery house?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when time or condition is the main problem, not the last dollar. In Montgomery that tends to mean one of these situations:

  • An inherited house with deferred repairs, such as an old roof or failing air conditioning.
  • A rental with a tenant, past-due rent or damage that would scare off financed buyers.
  • A military or state job relocation with a fixed report date.
  • A house with a pending tax bill, code notice or other cost the owner wants to stop.

A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, so repairs and cleaning are not required before closing. The tradeoff is that an as-is offer usually comes in below a fully repaired retail sale, so compare it against what a listing would net after repairs, commissions and months of carrying costs. We make offers on Montgomery houses and you are free to say no.

faqs.q: Is Montgomery the capital of Alabama?
faqs.a: Yes. Montgomery became the state capital on January 28, 1846, when the seat of government moved from Tuscaloosa. It is also the county seat of Montgomery County.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue. Your county tax office can confirm the amount and the payoff for a closing.

faqs.q: What tax is paid when a deed is recorded in Montgomery?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed under Code section 40-22-1, paid to the probate office before the deed is recorded. A recording fee is added on top, and the exact total depends on the sale price.

faqs.q: Does the weather matter when selling a house in Montgomery?
faqs.a: Yes. Long hot summers, spring hail and heavy rain wear roofs, air conditioners and crawl spaces, so those items draw attention in an inspection. An as-is cash sale avoids having to fix them first.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Montgomery house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses in their current condition, including those with old roofs, water damage or deferred maintenance. The offer reflects the repairs the buyer will take on.
